newsitem.title: UK: Dirty tankers steady but sentiment turning bearish.
newsitem.headline: Dirty tankers steady but sentiment turning bearish.

text.p: LONDON, Oct 15 (Reuter) Dirty tanker freight rates held steady for October voyages but longer term sentiment was more bearish on Tuesday with demand for tonnage in several regions beginning to slow down, brokers said.

West African markets continued to see moderate activity with demand for vessels to the Far East expected to pick up -- according to spot oil traders -- although there was little evidence of this so far, ship brokers said.
The demand was seen stemming mainly from South Korea where its Yukong refinery began commerecial production last weekend.
Yukong was seen buying a combination Forcados/Bonny light cargo on the spot market today.

Brokers said strong demand for West African distillate-rich crudes, particularly from European refiners had also boosted trade to UKC and USAC-Gulf regions recently. VLCC rates to UKC were pegged around W62.5 with USG voyages asking W65

Suezmax cargoes were fixed for Spain at W112.5 by a Spanish refiner and to the US Gulf at W104.5 for Oct 29 and W101.25 for Nov one. Brokers see rates for West African markets easing in the longer term as demand begins to slow and with better vessel availablity seen around mid-November.
"If you want prompt tonnage you still have to pay up for it but I don't think it's going to go any higher," a broker said.
Med/Black Sea rates were also seen easing as quick turnround trips and slowing demand saw more tannage becoming available.
However, for prompt voyages cross med rates for Aframax tonnage were valued around W100 while Suezmax tonnage took a steady W92.5
Inter UK/Cont activity continued active with Aframax tonnage valued steady around W110 and a ULCC fixed for Oct 25 from Sullom Voe to the U.S. Gulf at W52.5 by a trading house.
